slots_and_copies.name: active_record
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: No second populated region or redundant copy found anywhere in the 8192-byte file; only one 84-byte non-erased span exists. No slot-selection logic was found in the traced code (no caller of the save-write entry point was recovered).

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA kick-off + busy-wait primitive: loads src/dst/count+enable-bit into three consecutive global slots matching SAD/DAD/CNT_L_CNT_H layout (enable = bit31 of combined word = bit15 of CNT_H), then polls a status halfword for bit 0x8000 to clear. Not EEPROM-specific; shared by both the block-read and block-write paths with destination 0xD000000.

EEPROM block read (MMIO seed). Issues a bit-serial read-request stream via FUN_08084c70 to 0xD000000, then DMAs 68 halfwords back and unpacks 4x16-bit words by shifting in one bit per received halfword, producing one 8-byte block.

EEPROM block write (MMIO seed). Packs an 8-byte buffer plus block address into a bit-serial write-request stream, DMAs it to 0xD000000 wrapped in FUN_08084ba4/FUN_08084c2c critical-section calls, then busy-waits on the EEPROM ready bit (uRam0d000000 & 1).

Enters a critical section / enqueues a 3-field descriptor into what reads as a circular pending-DMA-request queue; sets a busy/armed flag to 1. Called immediately before the write DMA in FUN_08084da0.
Mirror-image teardown of FUN_08084ba4: clears the busy flag, unlinks the queue node, clears an enable-mask bit.

Read-back verification, not a checksum algorithm: calls FUN_08084cf0 to re-read the just-written block and compares it halfword-by-halfword (4 words) against the expected buffer; returns 0x8000 on mismatch, 0 on match. Labeled 'checksum' role only because it is the sole integrity-check mechanism found; it performs direct comparison, not a hash/sum.

Top-level write-with-verify-and-retry (up to 3 attempts): FUN_08084da0 then FUN_08084e7c, retrying on failure. NO CALLER FOUND anywhere in the 266-function traced corpus (ghidra/callgraph.json reports callers: [] and no other address in ghidra/decompiled.c references 0x08084ed4). The game-logic layer that decides what/when to save is not present in this workspace.

open_questions: No caller of FUN_08084ed4 (top-level EEPROM write+verify+retry) exists anywhere in the 266-function traced corpus; the game-logic trigger and in-RAM save struct producer are entirely unmapped.
No EWRAM (0x02xxxxxx) or IWRAM (0x03xxxxxx) address is referenced by any traced function, so no RAM mirror address could be assigned to any field.
No checksum/CRC/magic-signature routine was found; integrity may rely solely on the hardware write-verify-retry, or may live in untraced code.
Only one non-blank .sav sample exists, making it impossible to distinguish fixed-format fields from coincidental zero/constant values, or to observe any sequence/generation counter advancing.

The active record's true start/end boundaries are unconfirmed: bytes 0x1000-0x1003 (just before the observed diff) and 0x1058 onward (just after) are both still erased in the only non-blank sample and could belong to the same logical record or to adjacent, never-yet-written structures.
Whether this title uses more than one save slot cannot be determined; no second populated region exists in either sample, and no slot-selection code was traced.

The exact DMA channel used for EEPROM transfers (FUN_08084c70) is inferred from SAD/DAD/CNT register-layout structure, not from a resolved MMIO symbol name, since Ghidra did not label any of the _DAT_* globals involved.
